research_question: After an upstream decision changes, which dependent inputs, task requirements and reviews must be invalidated, and how does a multi-step task return to a valid completion path without losing independent work?
known_coverage: R02 covered one conditional address branch, active payload/errors and review invalidation. Multi-step dependency changes and completion based on currently required work remain outside its direct tests.
starting_sources: Reuse existing B-S205 check-answers capture first. Search current official conditional-step/task-list guidance independently; record only newly needed sections or sources.
candidate_policy: Prefer revising B-IU-006 if conditions have the same meaning. Register a new unit only if a distinct actionable decision is demonstrated.
proposed_validation_questions: Does changing an upstream answer invalidate only affected downstream inputs and approvals?
Can newly required work prevent completion even if every old step was previously visited?
Are inactive retained values excluded from effective decisions/payload without erasing unrelated work?
Does returning from a changed answer lead to the next necessary question and then review?
Are already-applied side effects retained as facts and handed to compensation rules instead of silently undone?
scope_boundary: B owns task dependencies and completion. A owns information architecture; C owns component/routing implementation; D owns broader efficacy methodology.
